_default: No type-specific description is available yet for {type} signatures.

STATIC.description: A file fingerprint checked against its size, partial checksums, and a strong hash.

PEHSTR.description: A PE string signature matches weighted byte or text patterns in a Windows executable.

PEHSTR_EXT.description: An extended PE string signature matches weighted patterns with extended PE-specific metadata.

DEXHSTR_EXT.description: A DEX string signature matches weighted patterns in Android Dalvik executable strings.

CMDHSTR_EXT.description: A command-line string signature matches weighted patterns against a process command line, not against file bytes.

CMDHSTR_FAST_EXT.description: The fast-path variant of a command-line string signature; same record layout and patterns.

AAGGREGATOR.description: A legacy aggregator stores the same boolean expression as AAGGREGATOREX, but as plain text instead of an obfuscated body. It combines references to other Defender signatures and is not a file pattern.

AAGGREGATOREX.description: An extended aggregator combines other signature results with a boolean expression.

VERSIONCHECK.description: A version check gates subsequent signature records based on an environment or engine value. It is not a detection: it only decides whether the records that follow it are loaded.

SIGTREE.description: A behavior signature tree represents related nodes, edges, and conditions used to identify behavior.

SIGTREE_EXT.description: An extended behavior signature tree records nodes, edges, and additional conditions.

SIGTREE_BM.description: A behavior-monitoring signature tree describes behavior rules in the BM format.

NID.description: A NID is a numeric reference into Defender's internal name or object table, not a detector.

NID64.description: A NID64 is a 64-bit reference into Defender's internal id table, not a detector. Packed record-id keys are resolved to the record they point at.

SNID.description: An SNID references a shared signature record and does not contain the record body itself.

REVOKED_CERTIFICATE.description: A revoked-certificate signature identifies a certificate thumbprint that Defender no longer trusts.

NSCRIPT_SP.description: A compact script-content condition: two hashes of normalised script fragments plus the matched window length.

NSCRIPT_NORMAL.description: A general script-content condition list: hash pairs and/or a rolling-window hash of normalised script text.

NSCRIPT_BRUTE.description: A readable script-content signature: normalised script text with wildcards, plus a script-type restriction and search direction.

CKSIMPLEREC.description: A checksum-region file check: literal first four bytes, a header CRC-32, and one region CRC-32.

CKOLDREC.description: An older two-region file check: two explicit offset/length windows with CRC-32 values.

MACRO_SOURCE.description: A macro source signature: an ordered sequence of one-way hashes of normalised macro/VBA routines for a specific macro stream kind. The hashes cannot be converted back to macro text, but can be compared across detections.

MACRO_PCODE.description: A legacy macro p-code fingerprint: three 32-bit routine keys derived from the normalised VBA p-code of a module. It is a structural family signature, not a byte pattern.

MACRO_PCODE64.description: A macro p-code fingerprint: three 64-bit routine keys (CRC-32, CRC-16 and length) derived from the normalised VBA p-code of a module. It is a structural family signature, not a byte pattern.

LUASTANDALONE.description: A standalone MpLua script: precompiled Lua detection logic plus the engine phase it runs in. It is a script, not a file pattern.

FILEPATH.description: A file path signature: a known-folder root (CSIDL or engine pseudo-folder) plus a case-insensitive path or glob pattern.

FOLDERNAME.description: A folder path signature: a known-folder root plus a case-insensitive directory path or glob pattern.

KPAT.description: A key pattern: a literal 8-byte anchor plus a byte pattern in which 0x90 matches any single byte. It is scanned against boot sectors, memory, decompressed buffers and macro data, not against one file format.

KPATEX.description: An extended key pattern: the same literal 8-byte anchor plus a pattern using the engine's 0x90 wildcard language (skips, ranges, byte classes).

VDLL_X86.description: A 32-bit virtual DLL: a complete PE image used by Defender's emulator to intercept calls to an emulated Windows module. The export name identifies the module.

VDLL_X64.description: A 64-bit virtual DLL: a complete PE image used by Defender's emulator to intercept calls to an emulated Windows module. The export name identifies the module.

KVIR32.description: A legacy two-window CRC page fingerprint: a 16-byte anchor at page offset 0, 16 or 32 plus a body window CRC. Mostly used for packer and entry-point code fingerprints, not as a byte pattern.

REGKEY.description: A registry condition: a hive, a key path, an optional value name and optional expected value data. It is evaluated against the live registry, not against file bytes.
